deployment_model: One customer, one dedicated WMS installation, database and server. Organizations and warehouses are business scopes inside that installation.

claims.boundary: PostgreSQL process termination and logical restore
claims.evidence: Actual owned clusters, no production data; final 3x10s result is recorded separately.
claims.does_not_prove: Physical power loss, controller cache honesty, disk loss, PITR or failover.

claims.evidence: Actual Go API/worker reject 7 unsafe settings; explicit transactions strengthen weak commit settings and preserve remote_apply; actual unsafe fsync reload refuses new writes.
claims.does_not_prove: A malicious PostgreSQL superuser, compromised OS or dishonest storage firmware cannot be prevented by application preflight.

claims.evidence: The synthetic dump preserves installation UUID and in-database hashes of bindings/key bytes, with actual API/worker profile probes after restore.
claims.does_not_prove: Production passwords, TLS private keys, OIDC identity-provider state, external app signing key custody, and OS service configuration are not backed up by pg_dump.

operational_acceptance_plan_not_executed: Choose customer-approved RPO/RTO objectives; record actual dataset size, storage characteristics, operator and replacement-host availability. No zero-error or zero-downtime promise.

Protect the dedicated server with tested storage write-flush behavior, power-loss protection and independent hardware monitoring. Schedule any actual power-cut drill only on separately authorized disposable hardware.

Keep encrypted backups and a continuous WAL archive outside the WMS server failure domain. Use separate backup credentials and encryption-key custody that SQL runtime credentials cannot access. A local dump on the same disk is not an off-server disaster-recovery copy.

For PITR use a valid physical base backup plus an uninterrupted archived WAL chain; pg_dump is logical and cannot be replayed with WAL. This repository has not yet executed such a physical/WAL PITR drill.

Before declaring off-server recovery operational, restore an independently downloaded/decrypted artifact to an isolated replacement host, with network egress and event consumers quarantined; compare private installation identity, keys, roles, migration receipts, per-warehouse exact decimal balances, active reservations, audit/outbox and command-ID witnesses.

Inject a missing archive segment, truncated artifact, wrong decrypt key, missing external secret, incomplete command witness and delayed archival; require refusal or a clearly failed receipt, not a passing summary.
Verify recovery at a selected timestamp/LSN using acknowledged command IDs and an independent witness cutoff. Measure archive lag, verification duration and loss bounds with the actual workload.
Document role/owner re-provisioning and external secret retrieval. The logical restore test recreates safe synthetic roles and reapplies reviewed grants; it does not restore pg_authid passwords.

Retain a last-known verified backup chain until a newer independent restore succeeds. Configure archive-failure, disk-space, checksum and recovery-readiness alerts; include restore rehearsals after migration/profile changes and on an approved recurring schedule.

A single dedicated server does not provide HA. Server/disk destruction requires replacement and restore; any availability promise needs separate replicas, failure-domain design and tested failover outside this current proof.
external_actions: No SSH, production service, real data, real key, off-server upload, physical power-cut or retention deletion was performed.
